subject: Transportation Systems
title: Light Rail vs. Heavy Rail
description: A short lesson to help you apply Light Rail vs. Heavy Rail.

hook.text: Light rail and heavy rail look similar. The differences are about speed, capacity, and separation.

buildup.text: Heavy rail runs on fully separated tracks—no cars, no pedestrians. Subways and elevated trains qualify.

discovery.text: Light rail can share streets with traffic, cross intersections, and run at grade without full separation.

twist.text: Sharing streets keeps costs low but limits speed and frequency. You can't run a train every 90 seconds through traffic.

climax.text: Cities choose based on demand. High demand needs heavy rail. Moderate demand suits light rail's lower cost.

punchline.text: Heavy rail goes faster. Light rail costs less. Pick one.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between light rail and heavy rail?
options: Light rail can share streets; heavy rail runs on separated tracks
